newsitem.title: USA: US Spot Products-Diffs hold steady, overlook API's.
newsitem.headline: US Spot Products-Diffs hold steady, overlook API's.

text.p: U.S. spot refined product prices sat near unchanged Tuesday as neither differentials nor the underlying NYMEX basis prices showed much movement.

The weekly inventory data failed to lend direction to the market, despite the American Petroluem Institute (API) reporting strong gasoline output of 8.25 million barrels per day and an overall build in stocks of about 600,000 barrels.
Distillate stocks jumped 900,000 barrels, putting the year-on-year surplus at 12.7 million barrels, according to the API.
On the NYMEX, July heating oil was up 0.18 cent and August heating oil was up 0.14 cent. July gasoline gained 0.02 cent and August gasoline firmed 0.16 cent.
U.S. GULF COAST
Gulf Coast differentials showed little movement in early action, as levels remained near steady with the late Tuesday marks.

Prompt regular conventional M1 gasoline was offered at 3.20 cents under the August NYMEX, slightly weaker on the day, though the end-July barrels were talked at about 3.50 cents under the August futures, according to traders.
Premium conventional V1 gasoline held its recent strength, with prompt barrels offered at 5.00 cents over the M1-grade gasoline.
Low sulphur diesel for nearby delivery eased modestly, traders said, with prompt barrels seen near 1.90 cents under the August futures.
MIDCONTINENT
Activity in the Midcontinent was extremely quiet with most players appearing covered for June, traders said.
Prompt regular gasoline in Group Three was pegged a quarter cent lower at between about 0.75 and 1.00 cents over the July futures.
Chicago was as quiet, a quarter cent down at 0.75 to 1.00 cents over the print.
Low sulphur diesel in both hubs were down about a half cent amid good supply. Traders pegged diesel stocks at 31-days of supply on the Williams Pipeline.
"It seems that right now the market is taking a summertime nap," said one Group Three trader.
NEW YORK HARBOR
Subdued trade kept prices near unchanged Wednesday, according to market players, with nearby barrels remained in ample supply.
Heating oil for prompt delivery sat at 0.25 cent under the July futures, while low sulphur diesel hovered near 0.50 cent over the contract.
Prompt regular conventional M2 gasoline remained between 2.75 and 3.00 cents under the July NYMEX, flat with the late Tuesday price.
-- New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1620
